text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- State-owned phosphates firm Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP) registered a better output and more exports in 1996.
- Interior Minister Driss Basri submits draft law on regionalisation to parliament's commission.
- Morocco signs support declaration in the first summit on micro-credits held in Washington.
- Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko pays working visit to Morocco, expected to seek military support to crush rebellion in the eastern part of the country.
- New arrests in Casablanca university after students stage demonstration in protest against recent trials and for the right to pray inside the precints.
- Morocco looks at resuming trade with Iraq under U.N. sanctioned "food for oil" agreement.
- Moroccan businessmen prepare return to Iraq.
- Visiting Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam says Syria willing to resume negotiations with Israel, on condition that the Jewish state keeps to commitments of previous government.
